findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary string values (e.g. "sent", "deleted", "poisoned") that are not valid ledger states
findings.failure_mode: callers construct LedgerWorkflow with any string for status, producing legally impossible or corrupt ledger states that bypass all workflow invariants
findings.fix: Replace with a sealed enum: enum LedgerStatus { New, Validated, Sent } with smart constructor and no arbitrary string construction

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set to any combination (e.g. is_validated=false, is_sent=true, or both true)
findings.failure_mode: callers can create a ledger that is sent but not validated, or validated and sent simultaneously, violating the strict lifecycle order New -> Validated -> Sent
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum carrying optional data: enum LedgerState { New, Validated { validated_at_ms: u64 }, Sent { sent_at_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a bare optional field separate from lifecycle booleans; sent_at can be None while is_sent is true, or Some while is_sent is false
findings.failure_mode: the three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at) are independently mutable, producing 2^3 * N_string unreachable/inconsistent state combinations
findings.fix: Fold sent_at_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum so the timestamp co-exists with the sent state and cannot be out of sync

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics; any string (empty, whitespace, arbitrary length) is accepted as a ledger ID
findings.failure_mode: callers can create ledgers with empty or malformed IDs; string equality is used instead of domain-semantic comparison
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `LedgerId(String)` with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and exposes only domain-safe methods

findings.problem: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly via LedgerWorkflow { .. }
findings.failure_mode: untrusted input bypasses all validation; no constructor enforces invariants so illegal states are trivially representable
findings.fix: Add a smart constructor `LedgerWorkflow::new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, LedgerError>` that validates the ID and initializes all fields to valid default state; make struct fields private

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LedgerWorkflow directly with no Result; it mutates status to "sent" without checking the current state is valid for transition
findings.failure_mode: calling mark_sent on an already-sent or invalid-state ledger silently overwrites status to "sent" with no error, producing duplicate-sent corruption
findings.fix: Return `Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>` with an enum like { InvalidTransition, AlreadySent }; check current typestate before mutating

findings.problem: all struct fields are pub, allowing external mutation of every field independently
findings.failure_mode: external code can set `item.status = "foo"; item.is_sent = false;` after construction, breaking any invariants the type was supposed to enforce
findings.fix: Make all fields private; expose only state-transition methods that maintain invariants

findings.problem: no benchmark or profiler evidence exists for the workload; mark_sent allocates a String via "sent".to_string() on every call
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics are unknown; repeated allocations in a hot path may cause measurable overhead
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom micro-benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocations and wall time; consider using a static str for the sent state

findings.problem: no cargo fmt --check, cargo check, clippy, or cargo test evidence provided for the crate
findings.failure_mode: the crate may have latent warnings, dead code, or compile errors not caught in this review
findings.fix: Run and report evidence for: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features, cargo clippy with strict lint gates, cargo test

residual_risk: The LedgerWorkflow struct permits any combination of status string, lifecycle booleans, and optional timestamp — all public and independently mutable. This violates every core Holzman principle: illegal states are fully representable, no typestate machine, no enum status, no newtype IDs, no smart constructor, no railway error taxonomy, and no encapsulation. The code is a flat data bag, not a domain type. Fixing requires replacing the struct fields with a typestate enum, a LedgerId newtype, private fields, a validated smart constructor, and a Result-returning mark_sent with proper transition guards.
